random_forest.name: Random Forest Regressor
random_forest.description: Ensemble of decision trees trained on 38 features (including pre-match career strike rate, in-game momentum, and run rate deficit). Averages independent tree projections to minimize variance under pressure.
random_forest.cricket_example: Chasing 180 runs with 60 needed off 30 balls and 5 wickets down. Random Forest evaluates thousands of similar historical match situations to estimate expected runs per delivery.

gradient_boosting.name: Gradient Boosting Regressor
gradient_boosting.description: Builds trees sequentially; each tree focuses on correcting residual prediction errors of the prior tree. Captures fine non-linear escalation as pressure indexes surge in death overs.
gradient_boosting.cricket_example: A bowler defending 12 runs in the 20th over. Gradient Boosting learns from prior death-over errors to estimate expected runs conceded.

logistic_regression.name: Logistic Regression
logistic_regression.description: Estimates the direct probability of a boundary (4 or 6) on the next delivery. Using balanced class weights and an optimized threshold of τ=0.49, the model successfully catches 71.0% of all boundaries in unseen play.
logistic_regression.cricket_example: Required run rate climbs past 15 with 2 wickets left. The classifier estimates the batter's likelihood of clearing the rope based on pre-delivery historical context.

xgboost.name: XGBoost Regressor
xgboost.description: Extreme Gradient Boosted trees with L1/L2 regularization and column subsampling. Effectively suppresses overfitting on extreme delivery outliers.
xgboost.cricket_example: Batter needs 45 runs from 20 balls. XGBoost predicts expected run output to measure runs added above expected under crunch situations.

lightgbm.name: LightGBM Regressor (Best Per-Ball Model)
lightgbm.description: Fast, leaf-wise gradient boosting optimized with 38 pre-delivery features. Delivered the lowest MAE and highest single-ball variance explained.
lightgbm.cricket_example: High-intensity chase where boundary frequency and dot-ball containment fluctuate. LightGBM efficiently predicts delivery runs with fastest inference speed.

over_block.name: Multi-Delivery Horizon (Over-Block [t, t+5])
over_block.target: Runs scored over next 6 legal deliveries
over_block.description: Predicts runs across the next 6 balls within the innings. Dampens single-ball discrete stochastic noise and explains 17.5% of variance.
over_block.cricket_example: Predicting whether the upcoming over will yield 6 runs or 18 runs under pressure.

comparison_summary.note: R² Score measures the fraction of variance explained by the model on unseen 2025–2026 data. LightGBM and Random Forest achieve the highest per-ball predictive power. Multi-Delivery Horizon expands R² to 17.5% by aggregating over-block trends. Logistic Regression is evaluated as a classifier (boundary vs non-boundary).
